particulars: All names, dates, places, store names, dollar amounts, heights, weights, print-point counts, sentence length, ages and statute names were dropped.

items.record: The case is a criminal prosecution for armed robbery that ended in a wrongful conviction: 'charged him with two counts of armed robbery'.
items.reading: A child-welfare agency's determination about a family, with a safety plan and supervised contact.
items.loss: The basic kind of matter and the institution involved are misidentified.

items.record: The conviction rested on a palm print and two cross-racial eyewitness picks made on a second look: 'selected no one on her first look and Brown on her second'.
items.loss: The evidence that produced the outcome, and how weak it was, is missing.

items.record: The physical descriptions did not match the accused, who had a beard and was thin and much shorter: 'Brown looked 'lighter' and 'smaller' and 'skinny''.
items.loss: The mismatch between the evidence and the accused person is missing.

items.record: A witness said police steered her toward the suspect's photo, and she insisted he was not the robber: 'an officer pointed to Brown's photo and asked whether she was sure it wasn't him'.
items.loss: Possible police suggestion during identification, and testimony against the official account, are missing.

items.record: The jury was divided and was pushed toward unanimity, then split its verdict: 'acquitted Brown of the Family Dollar robbery and convicted him of the Dollar Tree robbery'.
items.loss: The jury's internal conflict and the pressure applied to it are missing.

items.record: The examiner's report falsely claimed a statewide search had been run: 'Babb had never run the prints through SAFIS in 2014: they were loaded but never searched'.
items.reading: Says the record's truth cannot be known; treats the institution as giving a self-justifying but procedurally clean account.
items.loss: A specific false official statement at the root of the error is not recovered.

items.record: The state destroyed trial exhibits, and the courts excused it: 'no proof the clerk had acted in bad faith'.
items.loss: The loss of evidence and a failed legal challenge along the way are missing.

items.record: The case unfolded over years: appeal affirmed, an innocence organisation stepped in, the destruction motion failed, he was released, and then new discovery came.
items.reading: A parent or advocate pushes back and the matter stands at a threshold.
items.loss: The long sequence of failed and then successful challenges is collapsed.

items.record: The defence had to go around the police to get the prints searched: 'Brown's lawyers confirmed with the State Bureau of Investigation... that the three prints were still in the system'.
items.loss: How the challengers found a route to the truth by going around the uncooperative department is missing.

items.record: A database hit and an expert report pointed to another man and undercut the cleaning-product testimony: 'one of the three prints came from a man identified as Daris J.'.
items.loss: The new evidence that reversed the outcome is missing.

items.record: The examiner's wider work was put under review: 'the Durham Police Department had reviewed Babb's work as a print examiner'.
items.loss: Institutional scrutiny of a single expert's reliability is missing.

items.record: The state consented to a new trial and then dismissed the charge, while still defending the trial lawyer: 'maintaining that Brown's trial lawyer had been effective'.
items.reading: Predicts a procedural resolution in which the institutional record dominates, such as an upheld finding.
items.loss: The actual result is mispredicted: the institution conceded and the accused was exonerated.

items.record: The accused consistently denied guilt, pointing to his job and his custody of his son: 'I had a full-time job and custody of my son'.
items.reading: The parent depends on the system they are contesting; the family's crisis is turned into directives.
items.loss: The accused person's own steady claim of innocence and his circumstances are not recovered.
